subject: Priority SLA + Throughput Commitment for Q3 Renewal
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@avalonbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avalonbank.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — latency guarantee & throughput uplift

Hi Marissa,

We're coming up on our 12-month renewal and the execs asked for two concrete asks for the new term: a guaranteed 95th and 99th tail latency SLO for bank-critical endpoints, and a committed throughput uplift of +35% to support a new fraud model roll-out in Q3.

Can Redwood provide an addendum that lays out the latency SLOs, the throughput reservation, and what credits/rollback mechanisms look like if you miss the SLOs? Procurement also needs a draft to run through legal.

Attached is a snapshot of our projected traffic by route. Happy to set a call.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering
Avalon Bank

Attachment: avalon_traffic_q3.csv (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@avalonbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — latency guarantee & throughput uplift

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic snapshot. We can definitely do a renewal addendum that covers both SLOs and a committed throughput uplift.

Quick outline of next steps:
- I'll draft an addendum with 95th/99th tail latency SLOs scoped to the two bank-critical routes you flagged.
- Ben (solutions) and Monica (ops/oncall) will validate the feasibility of a +35% reservation and propose whether that should be a reserved pool or burst capacity.
- We'll include clear credit language (percent of monthly invoice) and a temporary mitigation path (read-only fallback and scaled model variant) for severe breaches.

Do you have a deadline for legal review? We can aim to get a draft to procurement within 3 business days if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — latency guarantee & throughput uplift

Marissa / Monica — reviewing Avalon traffic snapshot now. Initial feasibility notes:

- +35% committed uplift is reasonable if we reserve a dedicated burst pool with pre-warmed instances for 95% of peak minutes; that minimizes cold-start amplification.
- 95th and 99th tail SLOs depend on route composition (synch vs. async calls). We can hit tight 95th targets with QoS routing + KV cache priming; 99th requires headroom and a small safety pool.
- Suggest a two-tier reservation model: base reserved capacity (committed) + a smaller guaranteed burst pool tied to explicit pre-warm rules.
- For credits: propose sliding credits (5% invoice for single-quarter misses, 10% for repeated) + an operational remediation SLA (priority on-call, weekly incident blameless review).

I'll assemble a throughput_signature_matrix.xlsx that maps routes -> expected qps -> suggested reserved GPUs and pre-warm rules. Vivek, can you confirm that these pre-warm/eviction behaviors are supported in Private and Dedicated?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — latency guarantee & throughput uplift

Ben — confirmed. Platform supports pre-warm on Dedicated and Private with the following caveats:

- Pre-warm slots consume capacity even when idle; will need clear billing lines for reserved vs. active token usage.
- We can set hard eviction thresholds to protect 99th SLOs, but that means lower burst elasticity for non-reserved customers in shared pools.
- We'll need an ops runbook for the bank's primary on-call to shift traffic to the pre-warm pool during degradation windows; Monica, can you own the runbook and the weekly readiness checks?

Vivek
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@avalonbank.com>, Procurement <procurement@avalonbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft addendum and operational plan (attached)

Lena / Procurement — attaching a first draft addendum that includes:
- 95th and 99th tail latency SLOs for Route A (auth) and Route B (fraud-score)
- Committed capacity: base reserved pool + guaranteed burst pool details
- Credit schedule and a mechanized rollback/mitigation playbook (read-only fallback + model variant swap)
- Ops runbook ownership and on-call escalation path

Ben attached the throughput signature matrix; Monica will maintain the runbook and we propose weekly readiness checks for the first 12 weeks post-renewal.

Please review and flag any legal or procurement redlines. If acceptable, we can route this to DocuSign and aim to have signatures before your July billing cycle.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: avalon_renewal_addendum_v1.pdf; throughput_signature_matrix.xlsx

From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@avalonbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@avalonbank.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avalonbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft addendum and operational plan (attached)

Marissa / team — procurement reviewed the draft. A few negotiation points:

1) Pricing: Procurement requests a 6% discount on the reserved-capacity fee if we commit to the +35% uplift for 12 months. They want the discount codified in the addendum.
2) Credit cap: they asked that cumulative credits not exceed 20% of the monthly reserved capacity fee.
3) SLA measurement: they want us to publish the measurement dashboard URL and allow a weekly joint review for first 90 days.

We like the runbook approach and the credit sliding scale — asking for the two pricing/legal tweaks above. If you can confirm acceptance or propose a compromise, we can send the redlines back to legal this afternoon.

Carlos Mendes
Senior Procurement Manager
Avalon Bank

On Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 17:05 Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Carlos — acuity on those points.
>
> Proposed responses:
> 1) Discount: we can offer a 4% reserved-capacity discount with a 12-month committed uplift, and a 6% rebate if usage hits an agreed threshold for 9 of 12 months.
> 2) Credit cap: we'll accept a 20% cap on monthly reserved fee credits, but require a remediation plan before credits apply for consecutive misses.
> 3) Measurement: we'll provide the dashboard link and a weekly joint ops review for 90 days.
>
> I'll circulate a redlined addendum with these changes and a tracked DocuSign link. Ben / Monica / Vivek — please chime in if anything above is operationally untenable.
>
> —Marissa
